claims.text: Disaster recovery is getting a system working again after losing something it cannot run without, such as the disk under its database or a whole cluster.
claims.source_hint: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (Contingency Planning Guide): disaster recovery plan; glossary entry disaster-recovery

claims.text: RPO is the point in time to which data must be recoverable, i.e. the amount of recent data that may be lost, counted as time before the failure; RTO is the longest time the system may stay unusable after a failure until it works again.
claims.source_hint: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 §3.2.1 and Appendix C glossary (Recovery Point Objective, Recovery Time Objective). Note: course working definition; no pinned source in versions.yaml.

claims.text: The RTO period covers every step from the failure until the system is usable again (detection, obtaining a machine, fetching the copy, restoring, checking, reconnecting the application), not only the restore command.
claims.source_hint: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 §3.2.1 (RTO as the maximum time a system can be unavailable); lesson's step list. Note: course working definition; no pinned source in versions.yaml.

claims.text: Both RPO and RTO are set by the business (for example from how many orders staff could re-enter by hand), and the engineer's job is to obtain them, write them as checkable requirements and design to them.
claims.source_hint: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 §3.2 (business impact analysis determines recovery objectives)

claims.text: Lowering the RPO requires copies taken more often (more storage and tooling); lowering the RTO requires prepared machines and scripts and practised people; each step lower costs more, so the business that pays sets the numbers.
claims.source_hint: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 §3.2.1 (balancing cost of recovery against impact)

claims.text: At stage-2 backup-db.sh lines 11-12 run pg_dump on donhang with --schema-only --no-owner --no-privileges into /tmp/backups/donhang-schema.sql (out_dir default, line 7); captured output: 7 CREATE TABLE lines, exit code 0 (0 = the command succeeded).
pg_dump writes a database out as a file of SQL statements (a dump); with --schema-only it dumps only the object definitions (schema), not data, so restoring the file creates the tables empty.
backup-db.sh runs inside the lab box (line 5 re-runs it there via lab-run.sh), a container of the same Compose system on the same machine as the db container, so /tmp/backups is on that machine.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 scripts/terminal/backup-db.sh:4-5; docker-compose.yml services lab and db

claims.text: In deploy/k8s/db.yaml (stage-2, lines 50-60) PostgreSQL's data folder /var/lib/postgresql/data is the volume data of type emptyDir; the init-scripts volume (ConfigMap db-init) is mounted at /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d.
An emptyDir volume is created empty when the Pod is assigned to a node and is deleted permanently when the Pod is removed from the node; it survives container crashes/restarts.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Concepts > Storage > Volumes > emptyDir

claims.text: In docker-compose.yml (stage-2) the db service mounts the named volume db-data at /var/lib/postgresql/data (line 71, declared line 319); a named volume survives removing the container but is stored on the Docker host's disk.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 docker-compose.yml:57-71,318-319; Docker docs: Storage > Volumes

claims.text: The comment above the redis service in docker-compose.yml says nothing in it is the only copy of a fact (PostgreSQL has them all); the api's comment says it answers from PostgreSQL whenever Redis is not there; ProductCache fills Redis from PostgreSQL (cache-aside).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 docker-compose.yml:140-143,157-161; STAGE.md (Redis caches products through ProductCache, cache-aside)

claims.text: Only stores that hold the only copy of a fact need a backup; a cache that is refilled from the store of record does not. Deciding which stores hold the only copy comes before deciding how to back them up.
claims.source_hint: Condition: when the cache is filled only from another store (cache-aside) and the application works without it; docker-compose.yml:140-141,157-160

claims.text: Real data loss is measured to the last copy that can actually be restored; it exceeds the backup interval when a run failed, copied the wrong data, or was stored on the failed machine.
claims.source_hint: Follows from the RPO definition (claim 2); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 §3.4.2 (backup and recovery, off-site storage)

claims.text: With one dump per night, a failure just before the next run loses almost a day of data, so it cannot meet a 15-minute RPO; that needs a copy at least every 15 minutes kept off the database's machine.
